disclaimer: FULL RUN. OFFCHAIN-SIM. These numbers are the study's result and may be quoted WITH their label and their limitations: the human arms are MODELLED and not measured, the venue is one Aave-V3-shaped rule tuple, the liquidator is a testnet-shaped LogNormal(median 15 s), and nothing here is a claim about money on BSC mainnet.
label: OFFCHAIN-SIM

scope.design: Shock (4) x Clock (2) x Books (2) = 16 cells, crossed

armRoles.A: SurvivalGuard policy, unattended, evented. Decision-to-execution latency is a measured input, never zero.
armRoles.H1: REPORT-PLAN §3: a human always at the screen, no operational error, threshold rules, total event-to-broadcast delay U(5,15) s, +45 s per extra book, sequential. FULL RUN ONLY, and exploratory.
armRoles.H2: Real schedule, phone notifications, sequential books. Every parameter in H2_MODEL is published.
armRoles.H3: H2 with a hard 23:00-07:00 CST off window, forced regardless of the availability table. FULL RUN ONLY, and exploratory.
armRoles.P: Never repays, never closes. Measures whether intervening helps at all.

scope.confirmatory: C1 (Wilcoxon signed-rank on paired cost-inclusive terminal equity, A vs H2) and C1b (paired CVaR(5%)), Holm-corrected over the family of two that was actually run.

scope.chain: Nothing new on chain. BSC 56/97 only. Testnet U and mock tokens are never converted to dollars.

model.gap: Weekend rows cover 10:00–23:00 and 'weekend night = weekday night' (23:00–09:00). Weekend 09:00–10:00 is in neither row.
model.decision: weekend-day extended to 09:00–23:00, so the four buckets tile the day with no hole.

model.gap: Gives shock duration but not total path horizon, so the terminal mark would land exactly on the last shock tick.
model.decision: Each scenario carries an explicit settle tail (SCENARIOS[*].pathDurationSec) so the terminal price is a settled price, identical for every arm.

model.gap: The mock pool has no liquidation entry point and accrues no interest, so neither can be mirrored from the contract.
model.decision: Liquidation is modelled from VENUE_MVP (close factor, bonus); interest is modelled at borrowApr = 0, which is what MockPoolV2 actually does. The INTEREST event exists so the full run can switch it on without a schema change.

engine.gap: REPORT-PLAN §6.5 defines survival as 'HF never spent a block < 1.0 without a successful repay in that block or the next' but does not say who wins when a seizure and a repay land in the same second.
engine.decision: The liquidator wins ties. Scheduled events resolve OBSERVE, then LIQUIDATE, then EXECUTE at equal simulated time.
engine.direction: Against arm A. It is also the truthful ordering — a liquidation bot outbids a keeper for position inside a block.

engine.gap: A protect that is no longer eligible at mine time (debt already seized, HF back above trigger, buffer empty) reverts. A reverted transaction still burns gas — but a keeper that calls previewProtect first never broadcasts it.
engine.decision: The keeper is modelled as calling previewProtect: an ineligible protect is not broadcast, so it costs no gas and emits no event. Eligibility is re-evaluated at MINE TIME against the state the transaction actually lands in.
engine.direction: Marginally toward arm A, bounded by COSTS_MVP.gasCostPerTxN = 0.00751 N per avoided revert — 0.05 bps of opening equity. previewProtect exists in the deployed contract for exactly this and the Demo Lab keeper uses it.

engine.gap: The frozen constants in inputs/T1-liquidation-factorial.md do not give a cooldown, and the contract requires one.
engine.decision: cooldown = 0. The binding guard is the contract's own: protect() reverts unless HF < trigger AND the clamped amount is non-zero AND HF strictly improves, so an exhausted buffer stops the loop without a timer.
engine.direction: Neutral on the MVP paths. Verified: the buffer funds at most two protects before _clamp returns 'no buffer balance'.

engine.gap: REPORT-PLAN §3.1's availability table leaves several things open — where the notice clock starts after an OFF stretch, what happens to a notification in flight across a bucket boundary, and how many uniforms a call costs.
engine.decision: The engine does not answer any of them. `HumanAgent` in `human.ts` owns the human model and states its four decisions there; this engine asks it `respondTo(eventTSec)` and does nothing with the answer but schedule it. A second implementation of H2 living in the engine is a second implementation that will disagree with the first.
engine.direction: As documented in human.ts. Its decision 2 in particular favours H2, and therefore flatters arm A least, which is the correct direction for C1's own comparator.

engine.where: when a keeper decides, as opposed to when it executes
engine.gap: An arm that re-arms on every observation below the trigger would keep scheduling protects after its buffer is spent.
engine.decision: Both A and H2 gate on `previewProtect` — the contract's own view function — before deciding at all, and `executeProtect` re-runs every gate at mine time. Deciding on a preview and executing against live state is what a keeper does.
engine.direction: Identical gate for both arms, so it cannot move C1. It also removes the only path by which an exhausted buffer could burn gas.

engine.where: a broadcast protect that the market overtakes
engine.gap: REPORT-PLAN says nothing about what a keeper does when its transaction is already in flight and the position recovers before the block lands. On `wick-1block` this was not a corner case when the trough was ONE 3 s block: arm A's total delay is 9-15 s from the observation that trips the trigger, so its transaction mined at an ABSOLUTE 12-18 s of path time against a market that had recovered at 6 s, and EVERY protect A sent on that shock was obsolete before it mined. The trough is now 24 s with the recovery printed at 27 s, so A's protect lands inside it on every draw and this rule no longer decides the cell. (Two numbers that must not be confused: 9-15 s is the DELAY; 12-18 s was the absolute mine time under the superseded geometry.)
engine.decision: The engine re-runs every one of SurvivalGuard.protect's gates at MINE TIME and, when HealthFactorAboveTrigger now fails, treats the transaction as never broadcast: no gas, no event. That is the same rule as the previewProtect row above, applied to a window the preview cannot actually see into — the preview happens at DECISION time and the ineligibility arises between broadcast and mine. A transaction already in the mempool is mined and reverts, and a revert burns gas.
engine.direction: TOWARD ARM A, and on `wick-1block` it is worth the WHOLE of the pre-registered loss rather than a rounding error: A pays nothing at all on that shock and ties passive exactly, where charging one reverted transaction's gas would put it 0.05 bps behind. Left as it is on purpose — changing it after seeing that the pre-registered loss failed to appear would be fitting the model to its own forecast. It is a pre-registration decision for the full run.

engine.gap: MockPoolV2 prices are uint256 with 8 decimals; the generated path is float64.
engine.decision: Every price an actor sees is `oraclePrice(p)` — the path price rounded to the oracle's 8 decimals. One price, used by the pool mirror, by protectAmounts and as `priceAtEvent`, so the pool and the ledger can never be looking at different numbers.
engine.direction: Neutral and shared. Worth at most 5e-9 N per risk unit — the mock pool's own quote unit, not dollars — and identical for every arm, so it cancels in the paired difference. The terminal mark stays the raw exogenous path price via terminalEquityOf, likewise identical for every arm.

engine.gap: An event scheduled past the last observation of the path has no price to execute at and no window in which to be observed.
engine.decision: Nothing is scheduled beyond the horizon. A trigger crossed with no repay mined before the horizon (or before a seizure) is recorded as CENSORED, which is REPORT-PLAN §6.5's own rule for the latency secondary.
engine.direction: Shared across arms — the horizon is a property of the exogenous path. The MVP shocks complete well inside it.

verification.name: PRE-REGISTERED: arm A finishes BELOW passive on wick-1block, the shock that recovers
verification.detail: FAILED, for the SECOND time and for the same reason the MVP recorded. Median paired gap A - P is +1830.175 bps over 200 pairs: A is ABOVE passive on 72.0% of paths and below it on only 11.0%. A -35% wick crosses HF 1.0, so the trough that is long enough for arm A's protect to land is also long enough for the liquidator to reach passive. This is a failed PREDICTION, not a failed pipeline, and it is reported as one.

verificationNote: V11 is not a check on the pipeline. It is the pre-registered prediction confronted with the run, and a FAIL there is a failed prediction reported as failed — which is what a pre-registration is for.
